analysis: Both changed files are Swift test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Coordinator; no production source is in this batch. CoordinatorClientTests.swift (head lines 578-591): the backoff test now asserts exact equal-jitter ranges via nextDelayRange() (0.5...1, 1...2, 2...4, 2...4, with reset back to 0.5...1). This only tightens test coverage. CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift (patch): the header comments no longer say the suite is skipped in release CI, and the provider CI lane now runs it via scripts/run-provider-tests.sh. New tests cover a 1012 close reconnecting within 1 s, and a stable session resetting the backoff. A new helper (withGrownReconnectBackoff) and the CoordinatorReconnectPolicy(stableSessionDuration:) test hook are used by the tests, and makeClient gained a reconnectPolicy parameter. The mock coordinator's dropActiveWebSocket(closeCode:reason:) is also referenced. None of this changes the security controls in TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011. The tests invoke registration only through the mock and handle no real secrets or attestation material. The production reconnect behavior they exercise (1012 handling, a policy that resets backoff after a stable session, nextDelayRange) is not in the supplied evidence. Registration regenerates attestation on reconnect per the existing test at lines 70-90, so re-registration timing does not appear to bypass the attestation freshness model (the ±2 min blob timestamp and the challenge cadence). Remaining integration question: if the production change makes the provider reconnect faster after a 1012 close, then reconnect-flood or DoS pressure on the coordinator (TB-002 limitation: no pre-auth rate limiting) could grow, but that code is not supplied and no finding is warranted from tests alone. A reviewer of the non-test source should verify that the 0-1 s 1012 wait is jittered and bounded, and that only a coordinator-sent close code triggers it. The patch excerpt for the integration tests was truncated but covered the visible hunks.
